newsitem.title: USA: NuMed sees better prospects after loss.
newsitem.headline: NuMed sees better prospects after loss.

text.p: NuMed Home Health Care Inc said Wednesday it expects to improve its bottom line after posting a loss of $1.9 million or $0.38 a share for the fiscal year ended March 31.

"We'll do $26 million to $27 million in revenues this (fiscal) year," chief executive Jugal Taneja told Reuters. He added he could not yet project profits, but said "It looks good to me, no surprises."
Taneja added the company's monthly revenues are running at a little less than $2 million, up from a bottom of $1.25 million earlier this year.

NuMed attributed its fiscal 1997 loss to several factors, including a $900,000 contractual settlement it said it is appealing. Taneja also said attorneys and investment bankers cost the company about $400,000 in fees because of two aborted merger proposals.
The company received an unsolicited bid of $4.00 a share in April from a private hospital group, which was later withdrawn, Taneja said. He added NuMed got a second proposal, which was aborted too.
NuMed's stock traded at 1-5/32 Wednesday at noon, down 1/32 and close to its 52-week low of 1-2/16.
